import pandas as pd

# Load source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
source0_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_79/training_0.csv"
source1_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_79/training_1.csv"

df0 = pd.read_csv(source0_path, index_col=0)
df1 = pd.read_csv(source1_path, index_col=0)

# Operation 1: JOIN Source2_79_0 and Source2_79_1 on "city"
# Both have a "city" column, join on that column
joined_df = pd.merge(df0, df1, on="city", how="inner")

# Operation 2: group_by Source2_79_1.city, aggregations = avg(Source2_79_1.fare)
# After join, the "city" column is from both tables but identical, so group by "city"
# Aggregate average fare from Source2_79_1 (fare column)
result = joined_df.groupby("city", as_index=False).agg({"fare": "mean"})

# Ensure the schema matches target schema: ['city': string, 'fare': float]
# city is string by default, fare is float from mean aggregation

# Write the result to the target path
target_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_79/target_multisource.csv"
result.to_csv(target_path, index=False)

source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_79/training_1.csv", index_col=0)

# Join on city (inner join to keep only matching cities)
